survey_target: ATLAS+CMS searches sensitive to HVT Z'->WW, m(Z') < 500 GeV
survey_method: targeted web search (arXiv/Inspire abstracts) + direct WebFetch verification of title/abstract/mass-range + fetch_figures.py extraction of the candidate limit figure + visual mass-axis confirmation

Fetched by a prior stray session before this survey; not physics-relevant to the Z'->WW summary target. Left on disk under outputs/published/ins1734263/ for audit trail, not used.
Theory recast paper (scalar H->WW, 90-200 GeV), not an HVT/Z' interpretation and not a primary ATLAS/CMS search -- out of scope for this survey's model (HVT) and mass window framing.

excluded_from_gallery.id: dijet / Trigger-Level-Analysis low-mass searches (ATLAS TLA, CMS data-scouting)
excluded_from_gallery.reason: Generic qqbar resonance searches reaching down to ~375-450 GeV, but NOT diboson/WW-tagged -- they constrain a leptophobic Z'->qq incidentally, not Z'->WW directly. Noted as a caveat, not included as a WW-sensitivity gallery entry.

coverage_finding: For m(Z')<500 GeV specifically: ATLAS has THREE candidate results reaching into or below this window (2004.14636 lvqq from 300 GeV, 1710.01123 fully-leptonic from 200 GeV, and the superseded 1710.07235). NO CMS analysis found in this survey -- including the brand-new Jan-2026 full-Run-2 HVT combination (2601.12583) -- reaches below approximately 600 GeV-1 TeV in a Z'->WW-labeled curve. This is a genuine, surveyed asymmetry, not a search gap on our part: CMS's diboson/HVT programme leans on boosted-jet substructure techniques that require a boosted W (favoring higher resonance mass), while ATLAS retained resolved low-mass categories in both its semileptonic and fully-leptonic WW searches.
caveat_note: One WebSearch snippet (not a direct fetch) mis-attributed arXiv:2004.14636 to an unrelated ATLAS stop-quark search; this was checked against THREE independent direct WebFetch calls (abstract page x2, PDF, Springer DOI cross-check) which consistently confirmed the diboson semileptonic paper. Flagging for transparency per the number-integrity rule -- the survey trusted direct primary-source fetches over search-index snippets throughout.
